title: Dispatch: fail-closed record source-anchor gate so no compiler-authored record acquires SRD provenance by default (attempt 1)
description:
Implementation dispatch for parent eshyra-o9bd.19.1.3 (read `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.1.3`, esp. its NOTES and ACCEPTANCE). All design decisions below are made. If reality contradicts this spec, STOP, record findings with `bd update <this-id> --append-notes`, and close with a reason instead of improvising. Read docs/importer-fix-protocol.md first. Do NOT touch docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/freeze-manifest.json or add thaw notes.

GOAL: a compiler-authored record must not be able to acquire the SRD license/provenance block by default. Today every importer emitter in packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/emit.ts stamps `license: SRD_5_1_LICENSE` + `provenanceFor(page)` from nothing more than a page number, and no gate checks the record against the page it cites. That is exactly how table:starting-wealth-by-class (removed in PR #504) carried "SRD 5.1 p. 38" while no starting-wealth text exists in SRD 5.1.

DESIGN: a fail-closed, output->source RECORD ANCHOR GATE inside the importer pipeline.
Invariant: every emitted SRD record's anchor text occurs in the extracted text of at least one page its `provenance.locator` cites. The anchor is the record `name` by default; a record whose name is compiler-constructed must carry an explicit DECLARED anchor (printed text) with a reason, and that declared anchor is itself verified against the cited pages. There is no path by which a record passes without a verified printed anchor.

1. New module packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/recordSourceAnchors.ts:
   - `normalizeAnchorText(s)`: lower-case; map ’‘ to ', “” to "; map hyphen/dash variants to '-'; remove a hyphen followed by whitespace (line-break hyphenation); then drop every non [a-z0-9] char. (This is the normalization the supervisor's probe used; keep it unless it provably causes a false pass/fail, and say so in notes if you change it.)
   - `citedPages(locator)`: parse "p. N", "pp. N, M, ..." (list) and "pp. N-M" / "pp. N–M" (range, inclusive). Throw on an unparseable locator (fail closed).
   - `DECLARED_RECORD_SOURCE_ANCHORS: ReadonlyMap<recordKey, { anchor: string; reason: string }>`.
   - `assertRecordsAnchoredInSource(records, pages, { requireDeclarationsLive: boolean })`: throws one error listing EVERY failing record key (not just the first) when (a) a record without a declaration has a name not found on its cited pages, (b) a declared anchor is not found on the record's cited pages, (c) a declared anchor exists for a record whose name IS found (redundant declaration — remove it; the default must stay the rule), or (d) with requireDeclarationsLive, a declaration's key matches no emitted record (stale).
2. Call it in `runImporter` (index.ts, around line 2707+) on the FINAL record list that is written to records.json, with the extracted `pages`, and `requireDeclarationsLive: input.assertDeclarationsAreLive === true` (follow how that flag is used for relationship declarations). Synthetic-PDF importer tests run runImporter too; they must still pass. If a synthetic fixture legitimately fails the gate, report which and why in notes rather than weakening the gate.
3. Populate the declarations. The supervisor's probe (default rule only) found exactly 39 records failing on current main ddc231be: equipment:saddle-military/-pack/-riding (p.72); rule:armor-guidance (pp.62,63), rule:coinage (p.62), rule:oath-of-devotion-oath-spells (p.33), rule:the-fiend-expanded-spell-list (p.50), rule:weapons "Weapons Guidance" (p.64); tables: acolyte-bonds/-flaws/-ideals/-personality-traits (p.61), armor-of-resistance (p.209), circle-of-the-land-{arctic,coast,desert,forest,grassland,mountain,swamp} (p.22), confusion-behavior (p.127), creation-material-duration (p.132), cube-of-force-charges-lost (p.215), deck-of-many-things (p.217), draconic-bloodline-draconic-ancestry (p.44), half-dragon-breath-weapon (p.321), half-dragon-damage-resistance (p.320), reincarnate-race (p.174), scrying-connection/-knowledge (p.176), sentient-magic-item-{alignment,communication,senses} (p.251), sentient-magic-item-special-purpose (p.252), sphere-of-annihilation (p.243), staff-of-power (p.244), staff-of-the-magi (p.245), teleport-familiarity (p.186), wand-of-wonder (p.250). Reproduce this list with your gate before declaring anything and report any difference.
   For each, find the PRINTED text on a CITED page that the record is actually extracted from — e.g. the table's printed caption or header row ("d6 Bond"), the printed owner heading, the printed sub-row label ("Saddle" + "Military" style: pick a distinctive printed span such as the row text). Declare it with a reason naming what the text is (e.g. "caption-less table; printed header row", "compiler-named guidance section; printed section heading 'Armor'" etc.). The anchor must be specific to that record, not a generic word that appears everywhere on the page (no single common words like "Armor" alone if a longer printed phrase exists; prefer >= 2 words / distinctive row text).
   If a record's only printed anchor lies on a page its locator does NOT cite, do NOT extend the locator and do NOT declare an off-page anchor: that is a locator-completeness defect owned by eshyra-o9bd.19.2.2. Record each such case in your notes, add a note to eshyra-o9bd.19.2.2 with `bd update eshyra-o9bd.19.2.2 --append-notes`, and STOP (close your bead with a reason) so the supervisor can decide.
4. Tests (packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/recordSourceAnchors.test.ts), synthetic PageText only — no PDF extraction:
   - negative regression: a record named "Starting Wealth by Class" with locator "p. 38" over page text lacking it throws, naming table:starting-wealth-by-class;
   - a declared anchor absent from the cited page throws; a declared anchor present passes; a redundant declaration throws; a stale declaration throws only when requireDeclarationsLive;
   - locator parsing for p./pp. list/pp. range, and an unparseable locator throws;
   - every DECLARED_RECORD_SOURCE_ANCHORS entry has a non-empty reason and an anchor normalizing to >= 8 chars (guard against trivially-matching anchors).
   The real-PDF proof is the importer run itself (CI srd-importer-reproducibility runs verify:dnd5e-srd-pack whenever importer/pack files change); do not add a new whole-pack PDF extraction test.
5. Proof: temporarily re-add a fake record (e.g. push a table named "Starting Wealth by Class" citing p. 38 into the final record list in runImporter), run the importer, confirm the gate throws naming it, then remove it. Record this in notes.

REGENERATE + VERIFY: `npm run import:dnd5e-srd -- --pdf packages/core/sources/dnd5e-srd-5.1/SRD_CC_v5.1.pdf --out packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/` then `npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack` must be exact. Expected pack diff: NONE (the gate adds no output). Any pack change must be explained in notes. Run `npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root BEFORE committing (it rewrites files); if CLI suites fail on import, run `npm run build` first (fresh worktree has no dist). Memory is tight: use VITEST_MAX_FORKS=4 if tests time out.
Commit message prefix `eshyra-o9bd.19.1.3 `, ending `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
Completion report via `bd update <this-id> --append-notes`: commit SHA, the reproduced failing list, the declaration table (key -> anchor -> reason), the fake-record proof, verify results.

All 39 declarations verified against the real vendored PDF text (packages/core/sources/dnd5e-srd-5.1/SRD_CC_v5.1.pdf) before being written, using a throwaway probe script (not committed). No off-page anchors were needed — every declared anchor exists on a page the record's existing locator already cites, so no eshyra-o9bd.19.2.2 stop condition was hit.

Fake-record proof: temporarily unioned a synthetic record {key: 'table:starting-wealth-by-class', name: 'Starting Wealth by Class', provenance.locator: 'p. 38'} onto the real committed record set and ran assertRecordsAnchoredInSource against the real extracted pages (throwaway script, not committed) -> gate threw, message named exactly `table:starting-wealth-by-class: record name "Starting Wealth by Class" not found on cited page(s) (p. 38); ...`. Removed after confirming.

Synthetic-fixture note (pipeline.test.ts): the new gate (default-rule branch, no declaration needed) initially failed 13/44 pipeline.test.ts tests, all tracing to the SAME shared EQUIPMENT_PAGE fixture building block, on the SAME 3 record keys (rule:armor-guidance, rule:coinage, rule:mounts-and-vehicles):
  - rule:armor-guidance / rule:coinage are the same compiler-named-rule shape as the real corpus (declared anchors "Armor Proficiency" / "Standard Exchange Rates" apply globally by record key) but the reduced fixture's Equipment page never printed either phrase anywhere at all.
  - rule:mounts-and-vehicles's default name check failed for a DIFFERENT reason: the fixture's trailing "Mounts and Vehicles" heading line had zero body text on the same physical fixture page, so parseEquipmentGuidance's unbounded (best-effort, no "Mounts and Other Animals" stop present) scoop rolled the rule's sourcePage onto whatever LATER chapter's fixture page happened to follow (Multiclassing/Backgrounds/Conditions prose) -- a page that never prints "Mounts and Vehicles". In the real SRD PDF the heading and its intro paragraph co-locate on one physical page, so this never manifests there (confirmed: this record is NOT one of the 39).
  Fix: added 3 lines to the end of EQUIPMENT_PAGE (same physical fixture page as the "Mounts and Vehicles" heading) -- one real SRD-verbatim intro sentence for Mounts and Vehicles (fixes the page-colocation defect) plus the two literal declared-anchor phrases "Armor Proficiency." / "Standard Exchange Rates" (satisfies the declared-anchor lookups, which scan the whole cited PAGE's text, not just the rule's own captured body). Verified no existing assertion in pipeline.test.ts checks these rules' literal text (grepped first) or the mount/tack/waterborne table row counts (verified the 3 new lines don't match any of collectMounts/collectTack/collectWaterborne's header regexes). All 44 pipeline.test.ts tests pass; this is a fixture-fidelity repair, not a gate weakening -- no declaration was added or loosened to accommodate it.
